title: Cristian Mesquida
text: I defended my PhD on January 8th, with a dissertation examining the replicability and reproducibility of research in sports and exercise science. I am currently a Postdoctoral Researcher at Eindhoven University of Technology, where I conduct meta-science research. My current work focuses on Metacheck, an R package designed to help researchers prevent common statistical and reporting errors, promote best research practices, and extract data from published studies. I collaborate on this project with Daniël Lakens and Lisa DeBruine. My main responsibility is the development of the power analysis module and the validation of all Metacheck modules. In addition to my research, I teach quantitative research methods, including multiple regression, power analysis, and meta-analysis.

title: Teaching
text:
Currently I teach in three courses at Eindhoven University of Technology: Behavioural Research Methods 2 (BRM2), Behavioural Research Methods 3 (BRM3) and Metascience.

Behavioural Research Methods 2 (BRM2):

Covariate Selection in Multiple Regression: Exploratory vs. Confirmatory Approaches (Coming soon)
Introduction to multiple regression. This lecture introduces multiple regression analysis, including model specification, interpretation of regression coefficients, model assumptions, and practical applications in R.
Introduction to power analysis (Chapters 1-5). This lecture covers the principles of statistical power analysis, its role in study design, and how to perform power analyses for common statistical tests using R. The slides are available here.



Behavioural Research Methods 3 (BRM3):
P-values and Bayes Fctors. This lecture compares Frequentist and Bayesian approaches to statistical inference. Students learn how to interpret p-values and Bayes factors and perform Bayesian analyses for paired and independent-samples t-tests.
Advanced power analysis (Chapters 6-8). This lecture focuses on power analysis for more advanced study designs, including equivalence tests using the TOSTER package, factorial designs using the Superpower package, and simulation-based approaches in R. The slides are available here.


Metascience
Introduction to meta-analysis. This lecture introduces the principles of meta-analysis, including effect size estimation, model fitting in R, interpretation of results, and key methodological considerations such as heterogeneity and publication bias.
Bias detection in meta-analysis. This lecture will cover methods for detecting and assessing bias in meta-analyses, including publication bias, selective reporting, and risk of bias, using R. (Coming soon)
